payload.interpretation: Container/VM RESIDENT memory went DOWN (~3GB on the VM) while swap-USED rose +7GB. RSS-down + swap-used-up is the signature of macOS paging out INACTIVE memory to disk swap, NOT a process allocating more. CONCLUSION: the earlier pdf-extractor-runaway hypothesis (10:48Z) is CONTRADICTED — pdf-extractor grew only 250MB and the Docker VM came off its cap. The swap pressure is OS-level page-out, not a container leak.
payload.severity_assessment: NOT acute. Free 662MB and the OS just demonstrated a +7GB pool expansion (16384MB, blew past the 10240 cap) = strong headroom proof, the OPPOSITE of the pinned-at-cap VM-panic mode (project_host_memory_panic). Gateway/loopback HEALTHY. The relevant risk now shifts toward DISK pressure (the ENOSPC / LanceDB-bloat history) rather than VM-panic, since 16GB is now paged to disk swap.
payload.recommendation: ops/dev: the standing 'restart pdf-extractor to shed ~1.3GB' rec is now LOW-value — pdf-extractor is NOT the driver. This is macOS swap-management behavior, not a fixable container leak. Monitor disk free; if disk tightens, a full docker-compose down/up resets the paged-out footprint. No container-level action indicated right now.
